newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - BTPs vols hold but may drift off, eye CPI.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - BTPs vols hold but may drift off, eye CPI.

text.p: Implied volatility of options on BTPs traded on LIFFE held steady on Monday amid little activity as a result of a holiday in the United States, traders said.

But volatility was expected to come off slightly over the next few day's with the market anticipating a rate cut from the Bank of Italy once Italian consumer price data for January is released on Tuesday.
"The market has been relatively quiet," said a broker at a U.S. bank in London. "We've seen some aggressive trading of a March call spread but there has been very little else."
Brokers quoted implied volatility on at-the-money March BTP options at 7.19/35 percent, marginally higher than at Friday's close.
June vol was also little changed at 7.38/55 percent, but the back month had seen very little activity, traders said.
The main trade had centred on paper buying of the March 133.00/135.00 call spread involving around 2,850 lots, traders said.
Paper refers to institutions which trade for clients as opposed to locals who trade for their own account.
Near term, traders said they expect volatility to fall.
"It has been a bit high over the last few months, but will probably come off a bit over the next few days," said a trader on the LIFFE floor.
Italian consumer prices were forecast to have risen 0.2 percent for January, compared with 0.1 percent for December, to give a year-on-year inflation reading of 2.7 percent.
The market has already priced in a cut in interest rates from the Bank of Italy after the figures are released.
The Italian discount rate is currently at 7.5 percent.

"If CPI comes in at a reasonable level and we don't see a cut in rates you might see the market might sell off a bit," the U.S bank broker said. "And even if you do see a cut in rates, the market might sell off because it is priced in. It could be one of those Catch-22 situations."
At 1335 GMT, the underlying March BTP future was at 131.50, up 18 basis points on the day, having climbed to a new contract high at 131.75 earlier in the session.
